title: SearchAPI — Which One Wins?
objective: A security check confirms the account you're asking about is your own. The actual lookup doesn't agree with it about which account that was.

verifier.condition: The account endpoint returns a record belonging to a user other than the caller, for a request whose ownership check passed.

weakness: A request with a repeated query parameter is parsed into an array, and two different parts of the handler disagree about which repeated value wins — the authorization check reads the first occurrence while the data lookup reads the last — so the two checks can be made to validate against different values entirely.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /api/account?userId=&userId= (ownership check uses the first value, the lookup uses the last)
seededData: Users alice and bob, each with an account record. In-memory.

credentials.label: User account
credentials.note: Requesting your own account id normally works exactly as expected.

hints: Request your own account normally, with a single userId value, and confirm it works as expected.
A query string parameter isn't limited to appearing once. What happens if you repeat it?
Two different pieces of code might not agree on which repeated value 'wins' — the one doing the authorization check and the one doing the actual lookup might each pick a different one.
burpNotes: In Repeater, add the userId parameter twice with different values and see whether the response matches the value that passed the ownership check or a different one.
